transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-16
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Acme Head of AI), Marcus Huang (Acme Platform Eng), Zoe Carter (Acme PM)

Summary (auto): Align on POC success criteria (latency, throughput, quality), workload sizing (tokens/request, QPS), and a cost model for hosted vs dedicated. Agree next steps for benchmark and timeline.

00:00 Jordan: Okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Priya our SE. Quick roll call — can you confirm names?
00:08 Lena: Yep, this is Lena, hello. Marcus here. Zoe as well.
00:12 Jordan: Great. Today we wanted to scope the POC — focus on cost modeling and unit economics, plus what workloads you want us to size and benchmark. Priya will cover the benchmark plan.
00:24 Priya: Hi all, thanks. Quick agenda: 1) collect success criteria, 2) understand traffic and workload shape, 3) recommend benchmark config and knobs (batching/caching/quantization), 4) timing and deliverables.
00:40 Zoe: Sounds good. For context, our main product does multi-turn chat summarization and a short-text QA endpoint. Latency is important for chat; cost matters for the nightly batch embeddings.
00:55 Marcus: Our infra is AWS, in us-west-2, and low-latency region matters. We're evaluating hosted vs Redwood Dedicated vs running a variant ourselves. Security-wise we need SOC2 and KMS integration.
01:10 Jordan: Noted. On success criteria, what would success look like for you after the 4-week POC?
01:20 Lena: Two things: quality parity with our current model — we measure with our eval set and human review (target: no more than 3% regression), and latency SLO for chat: p50 < 250 ms and p95 < 750 ms for request size ~600 tokens. Cost target is trickier — we have a budget of roughly $20k/month for inference for this product line right now.
01:38 Priya: Helpful. When you say 600 tokens, is that total tokens or prompt+completion?
01:42 Lena: Prompt+completion average about 600, with completions typically around 120 tokens. Distribution is heavy tail, some at 2k tokens.
01:52 Jordan: Okay — we'll treat average at 600, P95 at 2k. We'll use that for batching and KV cache sizing.
02:03 Priya: Quick Q on traffic: what QPS do you see at peak and steady?
02:08 Marcus: Steady is ~50 reqs/sec across product; peak bursts around 250 for a few minutes during campaigns. Embedding batch jobs run nightly — about 5 million texts, average length 120 tokens.
02:22 Priya: Great. For cost modeling we typically need tokens per month. With 50 RPS steady and average 600 tokens per request, that's ~2.59 billion tokens/month (50 * 3600 * 24 * 30 * 600 ~= 2.59e9). But that's if all traffic is sustained; with burst and lower daytime usage actual will be lower. Can you confirm if 50 RPS is continuous or average?
02:43 Marcus: That's average during peak daytime hours — not continuous 24/7. A safe assumption for sizing the POC is to model 50 RPS sustained for a 12-hour window (we can give real traces).
02:53 Priya: Good; we'll model both a baseline and a peak workload. Baseline: 50 RPS * 12h/day; Peak: bursts to 250 for 10 minutes. Also we'll size for nightly embedding throughput.
03:08 Jordan: On per-token cost, Redwood's hosted unit price for shallow estimate is $0.0004 per token for the model family you're considering (open-llms family) — that number is illustrative and we'll give a detailed spreadsheet. For Dedicated with quantized weights and batching optimizations you can see marginal costs of $0.00008-0.00015 per token depending on batch and KV hit rates.
03:33 Lena: That's a big delta. What's driving that?
03:36 Priya: Mainly hardware amortization and higher utilization. Dedicated capacity lets you tune batch sizes and run int8/4 quant where applicable; you also avoid the hosted premium. Also caching — prefix/KV cache reduces tokens sent to the model and so reduces per-token billable tokens.
03:50 Zoe: Can you clarify what you mean by 'billable tokens'? Do you charge for input+output?
03:54 Jordan: Yes, our pricing is per input+output token in hosted mode; for Dedicated there's a committed capacity fee plus a lower per-token or per-inference unit, we can show amortized cost in spreadsheet.
04:05 Priya: Example quick calc: if you run baseline 50 RPS * 12h/day with 600 tokens/request, monthly billable tokens ~50 * 3600 * 12 * 30 * 600 = ~1.3B tokens. At $0.0004/token hosted = ~$520k/month (gross), which is obviously above your $20k budget. That implies either model compression, heavy KV/prefix caching, or Dedicated (or a mixed routing policy).
04:31 Marcus: Whoa that's way above our budget — so we need to explore caching and batching. Also we have some templates and a lot of repeated context so caching might help a lot.
04:41 Priya: Right — real workloads often see effective token reduction via prefix caching: if X% of the prompt repeats across users, KV cache can reduce billable tokens. Example: 40% prefix reuse reduces billable tokens significantly. Also batching many small requests into larger vectorized GPU ops reduces cost per token. But batching increases latency; we need to balance to meet p50/p95 SLOs.
05:03 Priya: For the POC benchmarking plan: week 1 onboarding/access; week 2 baseline run (hosted, default batch), measure latency and quality; week 3 tuning (enable KV cache, increase batch target, try quantized model), week 4 validation and report. We propose to run three variants: hosted default, hosted with prefix caching, and Dedicated quantized.
05:22 Lena: Sounds actionable. For the evaluation: we'll use our eval set for quality (automated plus human review for a sample). For latency we'll look at p50/p95 under both steady-state and burst scenarios.
05:34 Jordan: We'll also include cost-per-10k-requests and cost per-embedding for your nightly job.
05:40 Priya: A quick note on batching knobs: we have two main levers — max_batch_size and max_batch_latency (the wait time before dispatch). For interactive chat you'll want small max_batch_latency (e.g., 10-30 ms) to keep p50 low; for embeddings or batch inference you can increase batch latency to aggregate many requests. We can recommend initial values.
05:58 Marcus: Any guidance on KV cache TTL and memory sizing?
06:02 Priya: For KV/prefix caching TTL depends on how often your prompts change. If your templates are stable, TTL of 24-72 hours is common. Memory sizing depends on unique prefixes we need to store; we'll estimate based on the traces you provide. We'll also recommend cache hit rate targets (e.g., >30% effective reduction is a good baseline).
06:20 Zoe: On security — we require KMS integration and logs forwarded to our SIEM. Is that supported in Private or Dedicated?
06:27 Jordan: Yes — Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS and centralized audit logs. Hosted supports encrypted-at-rest and SOC2 but for full KMS control you'll want Dedicated or Private. We'll include compliance docs in the packet.
06:38 Lena: For benchmarks, can you simulate our exact traffic (headers, auth)?
06:42 Priya: We'll run a synthetic driver that replays your trace and supports the same auth flow if you provide tokens or a staging endpoint. For VPC Private POCs we can run inside your VPC connector.
06:52 Jordan: Let's dig into some concrete numbers so you can see tradeoffs. If we assume baseline 1.3B tokens/month (50 RPS * 12h), at hosted $0.0004/token => $520k; with 40% prefix caching effective tokens = 780M tokens => ~$312k. With quantized Dedicated amortized cost $0.00012/token => $156k. Still above budget, so we need to consider sampling, aggressive caching, model distillation, or hybrid routing for low-latency paths only.
07:24 Marcus: Are those per-token numbers proven? I mean what's a realistic per-token for Dedicated?
07:28 Priya: It depends on model size, seq length, and utilization. For a medium-size open model in int8 on 8xA10G or A100 type setups, we typically model $0.00008 to $0.00018/token after amortization. We'll run microbenchmarks during week 2 to narrow this down and give you a concrete amortized number.
07:45 Zoe: Could we cap cost via rate limiting or burst credits?
07:49 Jordan: Yes, we can put route-level rate limits and burst buckets to protect budgets. Also Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/caching configs to fit a cost target; we'll demonstrate that in the POC.
07:58 Priya: For the nightly embeddings: 5M texts average 120 tokens -> 600M tokens per run. If you use a batch-optimized path (no strict latency), cost per token is much lower. We can estimate the nightly job separately and propose a dedicated batch pool.
08:15 Marcus: Ok that might be achievable within budget if nightly jobs use a cheap batch cluster and interactive traffic is routed to a smaller, more expensive pool.
08:22 Jordan: Exactly — hybrid routing is common: route latency-critical chat to smaller high-SLA pool, route embeddings to cheap batch pool. That reduces overall spend.
08:32 Priya: Benchmarks to run: latency under steady QPS (50 RPS sustained for configured window), burst test (simulate 250 RPS for 10 minutes), cache-hit simulation (varying reusable prefix rates), and embed batch run. We'll capture p50/p95, throughput, tokens consumed, and model quality metrics.
08:53 Zoe: For quality we need a human-in-the-loop sample. We'll allocate 200 human reviews across variants.
08:58 Lena: Regarding timeline — can the POC start next week?
09:01 Jordan: We can start onboarding next week if you can provide traces and access. Our proposed four-week plan:
09:07 - Week 0 (this week): finalize scope and share artifacts
09:09 - Week 1: Provisioning, access, baseline tests (hosted)
09:12 - Week 2: Baseline runs, gather metrics, initial tuning
09:15 - Week 3: Dedicated/quantized experiments and caching enables
09:17 - Week 4: Final validation, report + handoff
09:20 Marcus: Works for us. We need the security packet for our legal review as well.
09:24 Jordan: We'll include SOC2, KMS notes, network diagrams, and a short handbook on data retention.
09:29 Priya: A short note on benchmarking methodology: to estimate amortized token cost we run microbenchmarks with the same seq length distribution, measure throughput at target latency, and then compute token/sec per GPU. Combine that with instance cost to get token amortization. We'll attach a sample spreadsheet.
09:46 Zoe: For P95 latency targets, we need under 750 ms. Is that feasible for long sequences (2k tokens)?
09:52 Priya: 2k tokens push transformer workloads; p95 will be higher. We can mitigate with model truncation, streaming, or lower-cost variant for long-tail requests. We should instrument and define acceptable fallback behavior.
10:04 Jordan: Any other blockers?
10:06 Lena: Procurement — if we go Dedicated we'll need a procurement timeline. But first we'd like to see the POC numbers.
10:11 Jordan: Understood. We'll keep procurement conversations parallel. We'll provide a pricing matrix showing hosted vs committed Dedicated vs Private.
10:20 Marcus: What do you need from us to start?
10:22 Priya: 1) 2 weeks of production traces (anonymized) showing timestamps, request sizes (tokens), and distribution; 2) evaluation prompt set and desired quality metrics; 3) access or a staging endpoint for replay (or we can replay offline).
10:35 Marcus: We'll gather those and target sending by 2025-05-22.
10:39 Jordan: Great. We'll also produce an initial cost model with several scenarios: optimistic (40% caching + quantized Dedicated), realistic (20% caching + hybrid), conservative (no caching hosted). We'll share the spreadsheet.
10:52 Priya: One more technical detail — for Dedicated quantization we need to validate model compatibility (some models don't support int4 easily). We'll run model compatibility checks in week 1.
11:02 Zoe: Ok that makes sense. Anything else?
11:04 Jordan: Quick recap of next steps and action items.
11:09 Jordan: Action items: Jordan send pricing + benchmark scripts; Priya draft benchmark config; Marcus provision access; Lena share eval/prompts; schedule kickoff.
11:20 Lena: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
11:22 Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up in email with attachments and calendar invites.

End of transcript.
